speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This was because the tightened safe management measures under Phase Two (Heightened Alert) imposed a number of restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There were two Phase Two (Heightened Alert) periods, 16 May to 13 June and 22 July to 18 August, both this year.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: During these periods, dining in was not allowed.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Government decided to support through the Rental Support Scheme, or RSS for short.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The RSS is part of a broader suite of measures put in place to address the impact of Phase Two (Heightened Alert) measures.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These include the Jobs Support Scheme and the various COVID-19 grants.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: To qualify, they must be tenants of privately owned commercial properties and they must meet three criteria.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: One, they must be a small and medium enterprise (SME) or a specified non-profit organisation with annual revenue of not more than $100 million.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Two, their tenancy must have been entered into before 20 July 2021 if it is a fresh lease; if it is a renewal, then renewed before 20 July 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Three, their tenancy must be in force from 5 August to 18 August 2021 and they must have experienced at least a 20% drop in their average monthly revenue at the specific property during both the Phase Two (Heightened Alert) periods compared to the Phase Three period from 28 December 2020 to 7 May 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is not required for the two RSS payouts from the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Those payouts include half a month of rent for the period of 14 May to 29 May 2021, which has been disbursed starting from 6 August and half a month of rent for the period of 22 July to 18 August 2021, which will be disbursed in October.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If tenants meet the first two criteria, they will receive a Notice of Rental Waiver automatically from the Ministry of Law (MinLaw) in the first half of October 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Tenants who do not receive a Notice but assess that they meet all the criteria can make a manual application.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will announce, in due course, the date on which applications open and other administrative details.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If the tenant also meets the third criterion – that is, a 20% drop in revenue – then the tenant will not be liable to pay rent in respect of the period of 5 August to 18 August 2021 provided that the tenant sends a copy of the Notice and proof of the revenue drop to the immediate landlord within 28 calendar days of the date of the Notice.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This can be done via email, which is preferred, to minimise potential disputes between landlords and tenants, or registered mail.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If the rent has already been paid, the equivalent amount can be offset against their next rental payment.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In designing the framework, we also considered the interests of landlords.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We recognise that some landlords have been proactive.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They provided assistance to their tenants in the form of direct payments and rental waivers.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These landlords can offset such assistance from the rental waiver obligations if the assistance was provided in respect of rental obligations incurred on or after 16 May 2021, which was the start of the first Phase Two (Heightened Alert) period.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Some landlords may themselves face financial hardship in having to provide the mandated rental waiver, for example, retirees who depend on the rental income for their day-to-day expenses.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They can apply for relief to be assessed by an independent Rental Waiver Assessor who will take into account specific factors in each case.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There will be objective criteria, including the annual value of their property and whether the rental income forms a substantial part of their total income.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If they meet the criteria, the Assessors can exempt them from providing the rental waiver.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There may be different circumstances on the part of landlords, which warrant special consideration, for example, landlords who gave their tenants flexibility and relief by providing short-term lease extensions with significantly reduced rent.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is not possible to define the criteria to account for all these circumstances in full within the legislation.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Hence, the Bill includes a provision to give the Assessors greater flexibility and discretion to take into account exceptional circumstances of landlords and to determine if it is just and equitable to make appropriate adjustments to the rental waiver obligations between the landlord and tenant.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Part 10A allows construction project parties to seek an assessment on the determination of adjustments to the contract sum arising from foreign manpower salary increases.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These amendments are largely administrative in nature to make clear that different application fees can be prescribed for an initial application for a determination and to allow MND to charge application fees for subsequent determinations made after the initial one.

speaker: The Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: With that, Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This is being implemented to assist small and medium enterprises (SMEs) during the recent two rounds of Phase Two (Heightened Alert).

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Under this framework, once the Bill is passed, eligible tenants can expect to receive a Notice of Rental Waiver and a declaration form distributed along with their second Rental Support Scheme payout in October.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The supporting documents include the profit and loss accounts of a tenant as evidence to show the drop in income.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I am concerned whether the requirement of strict profit and loss statement may be a little bit too onerous for some of the small businesses, especially those who may not have an in-house accounting or finance department or staff.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Separately, I am also concerned with the shortness of time given for the submission of such financial statements and I would like to ask the Minister whether there can be more flexibility with the time limit of 28 days.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Next, I also wonder whether the Bill in question could have been drafted to provide for the rental waiver framework to apply generally in future whenever there are changes in safe management measures (SMMs) like the onset of circuit breaker, Phase Two or Phase Two (Heightened Alert), with restrictions on dining in and other operating conditions on retailers of businesses.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We may not need to have a further amendment Bill to provide for a specific date in future when another similar Phase Two (Heightened Alert), for example, is called.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Perhaps this can be looked into in future, if necessary.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: They observed, "That the office leasing market performances in the second quarter is a tale of two halves.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Leasing momentum gets apace as business sentiment improves and more staff were allowed to return to the office." They then noted that this was then affected by Phase Two (Heightened Alert) in May and June, leading to work-from-home becoming the default again.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: They reported that the retail rental markets were affected by Phase Two (Heightened Alert) in this last quarter.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: CBRE noted that select retailers were snapping up choice locations in the second quarter.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: With such consolidation by so-called "select retailers" or even bigger players, reduced available space of choice for smaller retailers had caused their rentals to remain at elevated levels with weaker revenues due to prevailing safe distancing measures.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: If that is the case, I hope the Government will see how they can better support the SMEs and smaller retailers and businesses, prevent undue speculation by the bigger players and ensure that the playing field is still level.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: My concern is that SMEs, especially the micro SMEs, may still face business pressure and lower sales arising from SMMs and challenges of COVID-19 generally, and may struggle more with their business rentals as compared to other more established or bigger businesses.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Before the Member leaves, I missed the part on business rentals.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Perhaps he can explain that to me again?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I did not quite get the point on business rentals.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Maybe I will read it in a slower manner.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Just reading what CBRE reported that in the second quarter, select retailers were snapping up choice locations in the second quarter.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: And the concern I have here is: would the consolidation by the so-called "select retailers" or bigger players, reduce the available space of choice for the small players, the smaller retailers; in the meantime, while causing their rental to remain elevated with weaker revenues as a result of the current prevailing social distancing measures?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: If that is the case, I hope the Government will see how they can better support the SMEs and especially the smaller retailers and businesses, possibly, if need be, to prevent undue speculation by the bigger players and ensure the playing field is still level.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The framework also ensures fair co-sharing of the rental obligations between the Government, landlord and tenant.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One, basically, on those tenants who are having difficulties in terms of claiming the rental waiver.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They may be the elderly tenants, they are not IT-savvy and may not understand their obligations under the Rental Waiver Framework, like having to serve the Notice of Rental Waiver within a specified time in order to claim for the rental waiver.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Or they may not know what are the requisite financial documents because they do not keep proper profit and loss statements, for example.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In this regard, may I ask the Minister, whether MinLaw will be able to provide some guidance or assistance to this group of tenants should they face any difficulties in the process and, if so, how can they go about getting the necessary assistance?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My second clarification is that in respect of the assessment and determination which now includes the entire PTO chain, I think it makes an efficient and holistic determination by the Assessor of all stakeholders in the chain.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But may I get some clarifications on the approach to be taken if not all parties in the PTO chain had been joined to the proceedings or disclosed to be part of the PTO chain at the material time of the determination?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: All in all, I stand in support of the Bill and I welcome the Rental Waiver Framework.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, we made the processes as simple as possible and also the various resources to explain the scheme, including infographics; these will be translated into other languages.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We also work with partner agencies and industry associations to ensure that these resources are disseminated quite widely.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And webinars will be organised to explain the scheme to stakeholders and address queries.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The determination may affect the rental waiver to be enjoyed by all.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So the determination should be binding on all, because people can be affected.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Turning to the points made by the Member, Mr Dennis Tan, on the first point about tenants who may not be keeping detailed accounts, I think the starting point is that the tenants have to show that their income has gone down, business has gone down, from that specific premise.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I think we can all agree on that.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We accept that some tenants may not have kept detailed accounts, may not be able to show it in the way that the normal profit and loss accounts are kept.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Of course, even if it is not a profit and loss account, what they have must be helpful to come to that conclusion.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Otherwise, the question is, how did they know?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If they have other material, something to show that their business has come down and that is probative, that will be accepted.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It does not have to be a properly drawn up profit and loss account in the way accountants will understand.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Making a statutory declaration is a serious matter, but we provided for it last year and some people did do it.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If the landlord refuses to accept that, then it is a matter between landlord and tenant, and they can then go for assessment, too.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The final question is a much broader one from Mr Dennis Tan.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It is that he sees the market moving, consolidation by select retailers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I assume, by that, he means the more successful, perhaps the more high-profile retailers, and they are causing the rentals to go up and that is affecting SMEs.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: This is not a situation that arises only during COVID-19.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The more successful ones are prepared to pay the rental and that impacts on other retailers who may not be as successful and who are then squeezed out from, say, prime locations.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And sometimes, it is a cycle: if you are not in the prime location, then your business does not go up.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I sympathise with it but those are quite outside the framework of this particular piece of legislation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And that relates to really how you structure the market and what sort of approach we want for the economic structure.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Does the Government or Government agencies intervene to tell landlords what they can charge, what sort of tenants they can have or they must have a certain mix of tenants, whether we can or ought to do it and how do we make sure that SMEs have a decent stake in the business?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: How do you get to that is something that I am sure MTI and to some extent, MOF, will have considerably more interest than MinLaw has.      .
